subtitle: When a Name of Scorn Became the Mark of a King

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of a lone ruler before a great copper plate bearing an elephant emblem, misty Brahmaputra valley behind him
panels.action: Salasthambha stands tall on a riverbank ridge, hand resting on a massive copper plate engraved with an elephant, cloudy skies over the lush Kamarupa hills and the distant outlines of Haruppeshvara.

dialogue.text: In Kamarupa, after Bhaskaravarman’s glory, a shadowy figure called Salasthambha took the elephant seal—and turned the word ‘Mlechchha’ from insult into the name of a dynasty.

i18n.hi: कामरूप में, भास्करवर्मन की चमक के बाद, सलस्थम्भ नाम का एक धुँधला सा आदमी उठा, हाथी की मुहर थाम ली—और ‘म्लेच्छ’ गाली से राजवंश का नाम बन गया।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the Brahmaputra valley with rivers, forests and scattered settlements, dawn light
panels.action: Mist curls over the wide Brahmaputra as it coils past forested hills, scattered villages and shrines, smoke rising gently from thatched roofs in the Kamarupa landscape.

dialogue.text: In the seventh century, Kamarupa lay like a green crescent along the Brahmaputra—thick forests, river islands, hill tribes, and a kingdom once steered by the Varman line.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी में कामरूप ब्रह्मपुत्र के संग हरे अर्धचंद्र सा फैला था—घने जंगल, नदी-द्वीप, पहाड़ी जनजातियाँ, और एक राज्य जिसे कभी वर्मन वंश ने चलाया था।

panels.shot: historical montage, medium-wide: Bhaskaravarman at a distant court with Harsha, stylised, like a faded mural
panels.action: A mural-like scene shows Bhaskaravarman in royal robes standing beside Emperor Harsha’s court, scribes and envoys in attendance, the colours faded as if on an ancient wall.

dialogue.text: Bhaskaravarman, last of the Varmans, shone in northern politics—ally to Harsha, friend to distant courts. His death, around 650, left a throne without a clear heir.

i18n.hi: वर्मनों के आखिरी, भास्करवर्मन ने उत्तर की राजनीति में दमक दिखाई—हर्ष के साथी, दूर दरबारों के मित्र। लगभग 650 में उसकी मौत ने गद्दी को बिना साफ वारिस के छोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: close-up on a royal throne in an empty hall, dust motes in a beam of light
panels.action: An ornate but weathered throne stands empty in a dim pillared hall, a single shaft of light catching drifting dust as if time itself has paused around it.

dialogue.text: We do not know who sat next, or how many tried. The chronicles fall silent. In that silence, power shifted in ways our records can only hint at.

i18n.hi: हम नहीं जानते आगे कौन बैठा, या कितने ने कोशिश की। इतिहास चुप हो जाता है। उसी सन्नाटे में ताकत ऐसे बदली जो हमारे लेख बस इशारों में बताते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot from behind Salasthambha looking up at ancient stone fragments at Da Parbatiya, late afternoon light
panels.action: From behind, Salasthambha gazes up at richly carved stone doorjambs and pillars of an old temple at Da Parbatiya, vines creeping along the sculpted surface, sunlight grazing the reliefs.

dialogue.text: A later inscription names a new founder—Salasthambha—and a new line called Mlechchha, with its capital at Haruppeshvara near these ancient stones of present-day Da Parbatiya.

i18n.hi: एक बाद की शिलालेख एक नए संस्थापक का नाम देता है—सलस्थम्भ—and नया म्लेच्छ वंश, जिसकी राजधानी हरुप्पेश्वर, आज के दा परबत्य के इन प्राचीन पत्थरों के पास थी।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Salasthambha’s face in three-quarter profile, thoughtful, wind ruffling his hair
panels.action: Salasthambha’s face fills the frame, eyes narrowed in calculation and resolve, a breeze stirring his hair as forested hills blur behind him.

dialogue.text: We cannot see his first battle or council, yet his memory survives in copper and stone. The Hayunthal plates of Harjaravarman look back and name him their root.

i18n.hi: हम उसकी पहली लड़ाई या सभा नहीं देख पाते, पर उसकी याद तांबे और पत्थर पर बची है। हरजरवर्मन की हयुनथल ताम्रपट्ट उसे अपना मूल पुरुष कहती हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of hands unrolling a gleaming copper plate, engraved elephant seal catching the light
panels.action: A pair of anonymous hands gently unroll a large copper plate on a cloth, its surface engraved with Sanskrit lines and a bold elephant emblem that catches the warm lamplight.

dialogue.text: On the Hayunthal copper plates, centuries later, his descendant Harjaravarman orders scribes to inscribe their lineage under an elephant seal—solid, local, unignorable.

i18n.hi: हयुनथल ताम्रपट्ट पर, सदियों बाद, उसका वंशज हरजरवर्मन लेखक बुलाता है कि वे अपने वंश को हाथी की मुहर के नीचे खुदवाएँ—मज़बूत, देसी, अनदेखा न किया जा सके ऐसा।

panels.shot: angled close-up of the elephant emblem and a few inscribed lines, fingers pointing to the word ‘Mlechchha’ (rendered as generic inscription marks)
panels.action: The camera lingers on the elephant emblem atop the plate and dense inscription lines below, a pointing finger hovering over a specific word among the script.

dialogue.text: The plates call them Mlechchha—once a Brahmanical word for those outside refined speech and ritual. Here, it is not a sneer. It is a title carried with pride.

i18n.hi: पट्ट उन्हें म्लेच्छ कहते हैं—जो कभी संस्कृतियों में शुद्ध भाषा और अनुष्ठान से बाहर वालों के लिए ब्राह्मणी शब्द था। यहाँ यह ताना नहीं, गर्व से उठाया गया ख़िताब है।

panels.shot: split-panel style montage: on one side a Brahmanical scholar reading, on the other forest and tribal village scenes, both separated by a faint script line
panels.action: On one side a robed scholar reads a palm-leaf manuscript in a formal hall; on the other, a forest clearing with bamboo houses and a clan gathering, a subtle line of script dividing the scenes.

dialogue.text: Later scholars debate what this meant. Some see echoes of Mech and Bodo-Kachari roots, others stress a Tantric, cultural edge—marking those beyond polished court Brahmanism.

i18n.hi: बाद के विद्वान इस बात पर बहस करते हैं। कोई इसमें मेच और बोडो-कचारी जड़ों की गूँज सुनते हैं, कोई इसे तांत्रिक, सांस्कृतिक किनारा मानते हैं—शिष्ट दरबारी ब्राह्मणवाद से बाहर का निशान।

panels.shot: evocative medium shot of a Tantric shrine with lamps, skull-bowl motifs hinted but not explicit, a yogi-like figure in silhouette
panels.action: A dim shrine glows with oil lamps, a trident and simple altar at its heart, a yogi-like figure in silhouette seated cross-legged, the forest pressing close outside the entrance.

dialogue.text: Some historians, reading clues from inscriptions and ritual, see these Mlechchhas as weaving Tantric practices and local cults into the politics of Kamarupa’s old Brahmanical frame.

i18n.hi: कुछ इतिहासकार, शिलालेखों और अनुष्ठानों के इशारों से, इन म्लेच्छों को ऐसा देखते हैं कि वे तांत्रिक साधनाएँ और स्थानीय देवपूजा को कामरूप के पुराने ब्राह्मणवादी ढाँचे की राजनीति में बुन रहे थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a courtroom-like setting in an ancient Indian drama, all stylised, evoking Mudrarakshasa’s stage
panels.action: A stylised stage scene shows courtiers and a minister locked in debate in a Sanskrit theatre setting, pillars painted, curtains drawn back, as if from a classical drama performance.

dialogue.text: Vishakhadatta’s Mudrarakshasa, in a closing verse, hints at Mlechchha unrest after dynastic change—perhaps an echo, perhaps not, of tremors that shook Kamarupa after the Varmans.

i18n.hi: विशाखदत्त के ‘मुद्राराक्षस’ के एक अंतिम श्लोक में, वंश-परिवर्तन के बाद म्लेच्छ अशांति की सूझ मिलती है—शायद गूँज, शायद नहीं, उन झटकों की जो वर्मनों के बाद कामरूप को हिला गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Salasthambha in a council with mixed figures: Brahmin advisor, tribal elder, military captain
panels.action: Salasthambha sits on a modest wooden throne in a hall at Haruppeshvara, flanked by a Brahmin advisor with manuscripts, a tribal elder in simple attire, and an armoured captain.

dialogue.text: We must imagine the councils he held. A king from outside the old Varman line, sitting between Brahmin advisers, forest chiefs, and commanders, all watching how he would name himself.

i18n.hi: हमें उसकी सभाएँ कल्पना से देखनी होंगी। पुरानी वर्मन नस्ल से बाहर का एक राजा, ब्राह्मण मंत्रियों, जंगल सरदारों और सेनापतियों के बीच बैठा है—सब देख रहे हैं, वह खुद को क्या नाम देगा।

panels.shot: close-up of Salasthambha’s hand hovering over a blank copper plate as an artisan waits, tools ready
panels.action: An artisan kneels ready with burin and hammer as Salasthambha’s ringed hand rests on a blank copper plate, the first blow yet to be struck.

dialogue.text: He could have hidden behind vague titles. Instead, through his house, the copper plates would later proclaim a Mlechchha lineage. A word once thrown at outsiders, now etched by royal order.

i18n.hi: वह धुँधले ख़िताबों के पीछे छिप सकता था। पर उसकी ही कुल से, बाद के ताम्रपट्ट खुल कर म्लेच्छ वंश का ऐलान करते हैं। जो शब्द कभी बाहरियों पर फेंका जाता था, अब शाही हुक्म से खुद जाता है।

panels.shot: medium-low angle of Salasthambha performing a ritual at a temple near Haruppeshvara, priests and local devotees around
panels.action: Salasthambha pours water from a ritual vessel over a linga in a temple courtyard near Haruppeshvara, priests chanting while local villagers watch from under the banyan trees.

dialogue.text: The dynasty’s Sanskrit charters honour deities, grant lands, and trace their line like any other royal house. In form, they step into Brahmanical kingship. In name, they keep Mlechchha.

i18n.hi: उनके संस्कृतपत्र देवताओं का मान बढ़ाते हैं, जमीनें दान करते हैं, और अपना वंश किसी भी राजघराने की तरह गिनाते हैं। रूप में वे ब्राह्मणवादी राजधर्म में कदम रखते हैं, नाम में म्लेच्छ को थामे रहते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Haruppeshvara settlement with fortifications and a temple, elephants being led through the gate
panels.action: A fortified settlement at Haruppeshvara rises above the river plain, a temple shikhara visible inside as elephants, guided by mahouts, enter through the wooden gates.

dialogue.text: Haruppeshvara became their seat—elephants in its streets, copper grants in its archives, its rulers staking claim to both the land and the language of the kingdom they had entered.

i18n.hi: हरुप्पेश्वर उनका आसन बना—सड़कों पर हाथी, अभिलेखागार में ताम्रपत्र, शासक उस देश और उस भाषा दोनों पर दावा ठोकते जिनके राज्य में वे आए थे।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of Salasthambha on an elephant, overlooking the Brahmaputra valley, clouds gathering
panels.action: Mounted on a caparisoned elephant, Salasthambha looks over the sweeping Brahmaputra valley, dark clouds massing on the horizon as wind tugs at banners beside him.

dialogue.speaker: salasthambha
dialogue.text: If they call us Mlechchha, let the rivers learn that name.

i18n.hi: अगर वे हमें म्लेच्छ कहते हैं, तो नदियों को भी यही नाम याद हो जाने दो।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of a palm-leaf manuscript beside a modern scholar’s hand taking notes
panels.action: A modern researcher’s hand rests near an old palm-leaf manuscript and a facsimile of the Hayunthal copper plate, notes scribbled around words highlighted in careful ink.

dialogue.text: Today, historians like M.M. Sharma and Jae-Eun Shin pore over such texts, arguing over what Mlechchha meant here—tribal, Tantric, political—each line a clue, not a verdict.

i18n.hi: आज एम.एम. शर्मा और जे-यून शिन जैसे इतिहासकार ऐसे ग्रंथों में डूबते हैं, कि यहाँ म्लेच्छ का मतलब क्या था—जनजातीय, तांत्रिक, या राजनीतिक—हर पंक्ति सुराग है, फ़ैसला नहीं।

panels.shot: wide, timeless shot of the Brahmaputra flowing past ancient stones at Da Parbatiya, dusk light
panels.action: The Brahmaputra flows quietly past low hills as the carved stones of Da Parbatiya stand half-ruined yet firm, bathed in the orange hush of dusk.

dialogue.text: The river remembers more than our records do—Varman splendour, silent interregnum, the rise of a Salastambha house that dared to wear a name once spoken as censure.

i18n.hi: नदी के पास हमारे लेखों से ज़्यादा याद है—वर्मनों की चमक, बीच का मौन, और उस सलस्थम्भ घराने का उभार जिसने हिम्मत से वह नाम पहना जो कभी डाँट में बोला जाता था।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from the elephant emblem on the copper plate to a starry sky above, blending past and present
panels.action: The image begins tight on the elephant emblem of a copper plate, then pulls back to reveal it under the open night sky, stars glinting above like distant, watching eyes.

dialogue.text: Salasthambha’s story reminds us: power does not only silence insults; it can engrave them. When a despised label enters the royal seal, the struggle over who belongs is written into history itself.

i18n.hi: सलस्थम्भ की कहानी याद दिलाती है: ताकत सिर्फ गालियाँ ख़ामोश नहीं करती, उन्हें खुदवा भी देती है। जब तिरस्कृत नाम राजमुहर पर चढ़ता है, तो किसका हक़ है—यह जंग खुद इतिहास पर लिखी जाती है।

title_i18n.hi: सलस्थम्भ ने हाथी की मुहर छीन ली

subtitle_i18n.en: When a Name of Scorn Became the Mark of a King
subtitle_i18n.hi: अपमान वाला नाम बना एक राजा की पहचान
